tweet_summary: Post by 'StarPlatinum' (5.2M views) asserts 'Netanyahu is not alive', stacking circumstantial 'evidence': that Ariel Sharon's death took 8 years to confirm, and that a USAF C-17 'flying hospital' left Tel Nof on March 11 bound for Germany, supposedly matching an emergency.
why_note_decision: A note is warranted: this is a checkable death-hoax claim with high reach. Netanyahu is alive. He posted authentic proof-of-life cafe videos on March 15-16, 2026 (HaSataf cafe, Jerusalem, which confirmed the footage) and appeared at a March 19 Jerusalem press conference. The Ariel Sharon analogy is irrelevant (Sharon was publicly known to be in a coma, not secretly dead), and the C-17 'flying hospital to Germany' is unsubstantiated flight-tracking speculation that proves nothing about Netanyahu's status.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note affirmatively establishes Netanyahu is alive, citing his proof-of-life appearances (cafe videos c. March 15-16 2026 and/or the March 19 Jerusalem press conference) from a reliable outlet (Reuters / Snopes / Times of Israel / Al Jazeera / CBC). A strong note also neutralizes the post's specific 'evidence': the Sharon-took-8-years analogy is a false parallel and the C-17/Germany flight is unverified and irrelevant. AVOID the original note's failure (rated notHelpfulOpinionSpeculation 49, Incorrect 36, NoteNotNeeded 33): do not state 'he is alive' as bare assertion without nailing down a dated, sourced public appearance, and do not adopt an argumentative/biased tone (the original drew 23 ArgumentativeOrBiased + 12 SpamHarassment flags). A note that merely calls the post 'speculation' without sourced proof-of-life fails.

The note is terse and does not rebut the post's specific hooks (the Sharon analogy, the C-17/Germany flight), so on a hot conspiracy thread raters treated it as a flat opinion. Heavy brigading on this viral post likely inflated the NOT_HELPFUL ratings.

fact_check.notes: Netanyahu alive: cafe proof-of-life videos March 15-16, public March 19 press conference. He did miss a March 14 security cabinet meeting (chaired by FM Katz), which fueled rumors, but absence from one meeting is not death. The C-17 'flying hospital to Germany' claim is unverified flight-tracking speculation with no corroboration; the Sharon-8-years analogy is a non-sequitur.

importance.lens_rationale: 5.2M impressions on a head-of-state death hoax during an active war; flight-tracking pseudo-forensics lending false credibility to misinfo is a recurring epistemic-harm pattern worth correcting.
